qs.q: In a child with eczema, allergic rhinitis and pollen‑induced wheeze, which immunoglobulin is central to the underlying allergic mechanism?
qs.e: IgE binds to FcεRI on mast cells and drives the allergic cascade. The other immunoglobulins are not primary mediators of atopic asthma.
qs.s: Asthma and the Lungs: Understanding How the Disease Affects: MCQs

qs.q: A 6‑year‑old with eczema and allergic rhinitis develops recurrent cough at night. Which underlying pathophysiological feature links these conditions?
qs.e: Eczema, allergic rhinitis, and asthma commonly share type 2 (T2) inflammation; the other options are not described as linking these atopic conditions.
qs.s: Childhood Asthma: Clinical Features, Diagnosis and Management: MCQs

qs.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with eczema-like crusting, redness, and oozing of the nipple and areola that has failed to heal with topical treatments. What is the most appropriate next step to establish the diagnosis?
qs.e: Paget's disease of the nipple presents with eczema-like crusting and redness from an underlying ductal carcinoma and requires a biopsy. Topical corticosteroids would delay the diagnosis of this underlying malignancy.
qs.s: Breast Lumps and Breast Cancer: Triple Assessment, Staging and: MCQs

qs.q: A patient presents with a red, itchy, crusty lesion on the nipple resembling eczema. What underlying process is most likely occurring?
o: Severe fibrocystic desmoplasia around the ducts
Cancer cells from deep DCIS traveling to the skin
HER2 gene amplification directly in the epidermis
E-cadherin mutation causing single file infiltration
qs.e: Paget Disease of the nipple occurs when cancer cells from DCIS deep inside the breast travel up through the ducts to disrupt the nipple skin barrier. It is frequently mistaken for eczema due to its clinical appearance.
qs.s: Breast Carcinoma: Understanding Types, Receptors & Treatment: MCQs

qs.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a unilateral erythematous, crusted lesion of the nipple that mimics eczema. Which of the following best describes the underlying pathology associated with this presentation?
o: Benign inflammatory dermatosis secondary to chronic nipple friction
Malignant cells extending from underlying DCIS into the nipple skin
Primary squamous cell carcinoma originating in the epidermal layer
Lobular carcinoma in situ spreading through the lactiferous ducts
qs.e: Paget disease of the nipple is caused by malignant Paget cells extending from an underlying ductal carcinoma in situ through the lactiferous sinuses into the nipple epidermis. It is frequently mistaken for eczema but is consistently associated with underlying malignancy.
qs.s: Breast Cancer Guide: Epidemiology, Risk Factors & Classification: MCQs

qs.q: A 7-year-old boy has recurrent bacterial infections since infancy, eczema, ecchymoses, and a platelet count of 44,000. His brother and paternal uncle are similarly affected. Most likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Eczema + thrombocytopenia + recurrent infections + X-linked inheritance = Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome. Caused by deficiency of WASP protein involved in actin cytoskeletal functions affecting immune and platelet cell function.
